name: manual_518e74
claim: Before global heartbeat cleanup, stop affected workers, automatic restarts and queue mutations, and keep them quiesced until cleanup finishes; recheck the complete affected set under that maintenance window. If continuing quiescence cannot be established, do not run cleanup: the current implementation does not atomically recheck liveness before releasing each claim, so a restarting worker can lose its claim. When a peer stalls with a claimed queue task, verify the actual claimant and independently check claimed completion evidence. Only that live claimant may run queue fail <task_id> <claimant_id> --expected-claimed-at <claimed_at> --notes <reason>; it requeues only when retry_count is below max_retries, and queue claim cannot take an already claimed task. Never impersonate an absent claimant. Before global heartbeat cleanup, confirm all agents classified DEAD and obtain authorization for every affected legacy and queue claim; cleanup can requeue exhausted tasks, so hold unsafe or exhausted claims for separately reviewed authorized recovery. A reserved handoff retains required_agent_id and needs reservation-aware authorized recovery before transfer. Pass the claimed_at printed by your own queue claim. --unverified-legacy skips that fence: use it when your own stamp is lost, or in a takeover disclosed under the author-actor takeover policy.

decisions.notes: Corrects the command form in lesson_14ac09e1f380: since PR 525, queue complete and queue fail require --expected-claimed-at or --unverified-legacy, so the old command form is rejected. Older worktrees that share the queue database can still finish a task without a fence; the operator ruled this grandfathered by design on 2026-11-27.
